name: Email address changed
description: Sent to both the old and the new address when the sign-in email on an account changes, with the two addresses compared side by side and a window in which to stop it.

origin.note: Design: before and after — the two addresses set as a two-row comparison in an accented card, the cancel window stated as a deadline, and one action that stops the change.

subject: Your {{ product.name }} sign-in address is changing
preheader: Check the new address is one you control before it takes over.

heading_text.description: The headline. Say that the address is changing rather than that it has changed — the whole design rests on there still being time to intervene.

dual_delivery_note.description: States that both addresses received this. Without it the copy landing in the old inbox looks like a misdirected email and gets deleted, which is the one inbox that most needs to see it.
dual_delivery_note.default: This was sent to both the old and the new address.

body.description: What is happening and what to use in the meantime. People try the new address immediately and lock themselves out, so say which one still works.
body.default: The email address used to sign in to this account is being changed. Carry on using the old address until the new one has been confirmed.

old_email.description: The address being replaced, set in the mono face so an unfamiliar character in a lookalike domain is visible.

new_email.description: The address taking over. It is the emphasised row: a recipient who does not recognise it should notice within a second of opening the message.

current_label.description: Row label for the outgoing address. One word — the labels sit in a 30% column that still has to work at 320px.

new_label.description: Row label for the incoming address.

cancel_deadline.description: The last moment the change can be reversed. Leave it empty when your product applies the change immediately, and the deadline bar disappears rather than printing a hollow promise.

stop_by_label.description: Opening words of the deadline bar, joined to the date. Kept separate from the date so a translation can put the verb where its grammar needs it.
stop_by_label.default: You can stop this change until

deadline_note.description: What happens once the window closes. The consequence, not the mechanism.
deadline_note.default: After that the old address stops working for sign-in and for password resets.

cancel_label.description: Label on the one action. It is a refusal, so word it as one.

cancel_url.description: Where the change is reversed. Should work from the old address without a password — someone whose account was taken over cannot sign in to cancel anything.

no_action_note.description: The closing line for the majority who made this change themselves, and the route for the person who no longer controls the old mailbox.
no_action_note.default: Made this change yourself? There is nothing to do — the new address takes over on its own. If you have lost access to the old address, contact us rather than replying to this message.
